prompt: CHALLENGE: Why does a carboxylic acid show a VERY broad O–H band stretching from 2500–3300 cm⁻¹, while an alcohol's O–H is only moderately broad (3200–3550)?

options.label: In solution, carboxylic acids form H-bonded cyclic DIMERS with two short, strong H-bonds. The O–H in these dimers samples a wide range of distances/strengths, giving an extremely broad band. Alcohols form more disordered H-bond chains (narrower spread).
Carboxylic acids have higher molecular weight.

explanation: Stronger, shorter H-bonds give broader IR bands (the force constant varies more across the vibrational motion). COOH dimers have very strong 'double H-bonds' with large anharmonicity → extremely wide absorption. This is why the broad COOH stretch is diagnostic — no other common group produces it.
